Return the FRS identity and every linked program ID, preserving the source-specific permit and withdrawal namespaces. Do these sources establish current operation, ownership or another Hollingsworth site?
answer: The assessment’s Appendix D names Hollingsworth & Vose Co. at 112 Washington Street, East Walpole under MA0004570; the later packet uses Hollingsworth and Vose Company at the same address. Match FRS 110000310556 and retain all eleven original program associations: TRIS 02032HLLNG112WA; AIR MA0000002511900260; NPDES MAR053214, MA0044996, MA0004570 and MAPIU00J4; EIS 6567911; RCRAINFO and SEMS each MAD001006360 in separate namespaces; TSCA 114306; CEDRI CEDRI124226. The later fact sheet’s WMA 41930702 is a state withdrawal registration, not another national NPDES ID. Gasket-paper manufacturing is a historical source description, not proof of present production. Similar company names at West Groton and the Boston/Milton Tileston & Hollingsworth dam are not this East Walpole identity. Neither historical water packet nor registry name proves a transaction, current owner, permit status or actual process-discharge start.

evidence.quote: 1. Proposed Action, Type of Facility, and Discharge Location The above applicant has applied to the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) for re-issuance of a National Pollutant Discharge Elimination Sy stem (NPDES) permit to discharge contact and non-contact cooling water into the Neponset River (the designated receiving water). The current permit (“2003 permit”) was issued on April 18, 2003, became effective on June 17, 2003, and expired September 30, 2006. EPA received a completed permit renewal application from the facility dated March 13, 2006. Since the permit renewal application was deemed timely and complete by EPA, the permit has been administratively continued pursuant to 40 CRF § 122.6. The Hollingsworth and Vose (H&V) East Walpole facility is engaged in the manufacture of specialty paper (gasketing papers). In H&V’s basic papermaking process, natural and synthetic fibers and fillers are dispersed in water and paper making chemicals (latex chemicals) are added. The stock is then spread out on to a conventional paper machine. Vulcanization (cross linking) is performed to give fluid and heat resistance and physical strength to gasketing papers. Zinc is needed as an activator of vulcanization, and it is used in the form of several different compounds. Process water is withdrawn from the Neponset River and is covered under the Water Management Act (WMA) registration number 41930702. The facility is located at Latitude 42° 10’ 00” Longitude 71° 12’ 45”. An aerial view of the facility, Outfall 002 and the Neponset River is shown in Attachment A. 2. Description of Discharge The 2003 permit authorized two discharges from this site (Outfall 002 and Outfall 003). Outfall 002 is comprised of backwash from a strainer which is used intermittently to filter river water to be used in the manufacturing process. It is only used when the river water is determined to be of undesirable clarity to meet specific job requirements. The 2003 permit authorized an average flow of 4000 gallons per day from this outfall. Outfall 003, which was initially authorized in the 1995 permit to discharge treated process water from the paper making operation, has never been utilized. The 2003 permit authorized the discharge of an average flow of 700,000 gallons per day. Storm water discharges from this site are authorized under the Storm Water Multi-Sector General Permit for Industrial Activities (MSGP) with tracking number MAR05CV91, and so are not addressed in this permit. Discharge monitoring data from January 31, 2006 through December 31, 2010 for Outfalls 002 and 003 was collected under the terms of the 2003 permit. The facility did not discharge during that time period and the only data reported were pH (8.0 Standard units) and Temperature (73.8°F) from August 2007. No permit limits were violated. 3. Receiving Water Description

question: Build a source-qualified obligation register for the 2011 MA0004570 instrument at facility-005. Reconcile the 1995 process-discharge proposal, then state the issued outfall, flow/TSS/pH monitoring and the pH and NetDMR qualifiers. Are those historical conditions established as current?
answer: Keep the 1995 proposed process-water 0.7 MGD and strainer-backwash 0.004 MGD roles separate. The 2011 issued Part I table authorizes filter backwash from Outfall 002, with flow 4,000 gpd average monthly, maximum-daily Report, Daily Estimate; TSS 20 mg/l monthly-average and 30 mg/l daily-maximum with 1/Month Grab; pH 6.5–8.3 S.U. with 1/Month Grab. Sample at the strainer overflow tank after treatment and before the river. The pH footnote allows a documented natural-cause exception only with source and effluent measurements the same, no more than 0.5 units outside natural background, and documentation with the monthly DMR. NetDMR must begin within one year of effectiveness unless a reasonable technical/administrative basis supports an opt-out: advance written approval at least 60 days before the required date, valid 12 months from approval, then renewed approval or electronic submission. Electronic DMRs are due no later than the 15th of the following month; the specified MassDEP other-report copies remain. The historical proposal cannot add process-water limits to this issued table. Obtain successor permits/status and actual monitoring/approved opt-outs before asserting present applicability or a missed deadline.

The facility is located at Latitude 42° 10’ 00” Longitude 71° 12’ 45”. An aerial view of the facility, Outfall 002 and the Neponset River is shown in Attachment A. 2. Description of Discharge The 2003 permit authorized two discharges from this site (Outfall 002 and Outfall 003). Outfall 002 is comprised of backwash from a strainer which is used intermittently to filter river water to be used in the manufacturing process. It is only used when the river water is determined to be of undesirable clarity to meet specific job requirements. The 2003 permit authorized an average flow of 4000 gallons per day from this outfall. Outfall 003, which was initially authorized in the 1995 permit to discharge treated process water from the paper making operation, has never been utilized. The 2003 permit authorized the discharge of an average flow of 700,000 gallons per day. Storm water discharges from this site are authorized under the Storm Water Multi-Sector General Permit for Industrial Activities (MSGP) with tracking number MAR05CV91, and so are not addressed in this permit. Discharge monitoring data from January 31, 2006 through December 31, 2010 for Outfalls 002 and 003 was collected under the terms of the 2003 permit. The facility did not discharge during that time period and the only data reported were pH (8.0 Standard units) and Temperature (73.8°F) from August 2007. No permit limits were violated. 3.
